sections.text:
1 Has observationes ediderunt Bullialdus (Bouilleau), Astronomia philolaïca,
t. I, p. 172 (e cod. Parisino 2390?); Halma, Chronologie de Ptolémée, part. II, p. 10-
12. Cf. Paul Tannery, Bull. des Sc. mathém., 2e série, VIII (1884), p. 321; XVIII
(1894), p. 20. — Heliodorus hic, Hermiae filius, Ammonii frater (Zeller, Philos. Gr.,
V3, p. 829, n. 1), Eutocii magister, qui circa annum 500 Alexandriae planetarum
coniunctiones observabat, idem esse videtur qui in codicibus astrologicis Ἡλιόδω-
ρος ὁ φιλόσοφος auctor saepe nominatur et commentarium in Pauli Alexandrini
Εἰσαγωγήν scripsit. Cui commentario auctorem olim supposui Heliodorum che-
micum (Catal. Florent., p. 57), sed hanc sententiam non admodum credibilem esse
recte monuit Boll, Byz. Zeitschr., VIII, 1899, p. 525, n. 1.
sections.en:
1 These observations were published by Bullialdus (Bouilleau), Astronomia philolaïca,
t. I, p. 172 (from cod. Parisinus 2390?); Halma, Chronologie de Ptolémée, part. II, p. 10-
12. Cf. Paul Tannery, Bull. des Sc. mathém., 2e série, VIII (1884), p. 321; XVIII
(1894), p. 20. — This Heliodorus, son of Hermias, brother of Ammonius (Zeller, Philos. Gr.,
V3, p. 829, n. 1), teacher of Eutocius, who around the year 500 at Alexandria observed the planetary
conjunctions, seems to be the same one who in astrological codices is often named as the author Ἡλιόδω-
ρος ὁ φιλόσοφος ('Heliodorus the philosopher') and wrote a commentary on Paulus Alexandrinus's
Εἰσαγωγήν ('Introduction'). To which commentary I formerly supposed the author to be Heliodorus the che-
mist (Catal. Florent., p. 57), but that this opinion is not very credible
Boll rightly warned, Byz. Zeitschr., VIII, 1899, p. 525, n. 1.

sections.text:
2 Haec epitheta ex Dorothei Sidonii poemate excerpta eadem fere sunt quae in
codice Laurentiano XXVIII, 34, f. 144, sine auctoris nomine tradita et in Catalogo
Florentino, p. 172, edita sunt. Cum modo Laurentianus liber modo Marcianus
plenior sit, utrosque laterculos ex collectione ampliore contractos esse apparet. —
De similibus divinorum nominum indicibus, cf. Catal. Florent., l. c. et fragmentum
saeculi II vel III apud Wilcken, Tafeln zur älteren griech. Paläographie, 1891, tab. II.
sections.en:
2 These epithets excerpted from the poem of Dorotheus of Sidon are almost the same as those which in
codex Laurentianus XXVIII, 34, f. 144, are handed down without the author's name and in the Catalogus
Florentinus, p. 172, were published. Since sometimes the Laurentian book, sometimes the Marcian
is fuller, it appears that both lists were contracted from a larger collection. —
Concerning similar indices of divine names, cf. Catal. Florent., l. c. and a fragment
of the II or III century in Wilcken, Tafeln zur älteren griech. Paläographie, 1891, tab. II.

summary.headline: Heliodorus and Dorotheus’ Star Names
summary.text: Heliodorus records planetary observations from 475–509, including Mars touching Jupiter, followed by Dorotheus of Sidon’s epithets for the seven stars, with entries for Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars.
